v1_6_model_that_was_wrong.what_v1_6_drew: k_wrong ~ Binomial(n_A, true_share) and then reported the realised share as k/(k + n_refused)
v1_6_model_that_was_wrong.consequence: for the DEV cohort this maps 'true_share = 0.50' onto a realised share of about 0.85, so the reported false-positive rate of 0.0 was the rate at a true share of 0.85, not 0.50

operating_characteristics.corrected_model: per-participant error rates are scaled so that the realised pooled share equals the target; n_A, n_refused and the participant-level error rate heterogeneity are inherited from DEV
operating_characteristics.reading: the point-estimate rule 'share < 0.50' is a benchmark comparison, not a controlled test: at a true share of exactly 0.50 it fires about half the time, because the estimator is unbiased at the benchmark. It never fires when the true share is 0.55 or above. The interval rule 'the whole 95% interval lies below 0.50' is the variant with an actual confidence statement; its coverage column records how often the interval actually contains the true share, which is the calibration check that the point rule never had.

C5_E2_demotion.why: the v1.6 criterion ('the 95% interval excludes 0') has no valid Type I error control at n <= 5: the participant-level bootstrap percentile interval is not coverage-calibrated at these sample sizes, and its false-positive rate under a symmetric null was measured at 0.13 to 0.18, i.e. roughly three times the nominal alpha. Replacing it with an EXACT participant-level sign-flip permutation test restores the Type I control, but then faces the small-n reality:

exact_test.test: exact one-sided sign-flip permutation test on the participant-level paired log-odds deltas; all 2^n sign patterns are enumerated, so there is no Monte-Carlo error
exact_test.companion: exact one-sided binomial sign test on the number of positive deltas (no magnitude symmetry assumed)

6.rejection_requires: all n deltas positive, or n-1 positive with a single small negative

exact_test.key_fact: at n = 4 the smallest attainable one-sided p is 1/16 = 0.0625, which is ABOVE alpha = 0.05. No one-sided exact test can reject at n = 4 at all.

power.method: resample n participant deltas with replacement from the 16 observed DEV deltas; the participant is the independent unit and the real sign pattern (14 of 16 positive) is preserved
power.reading: the exact tests are far more conservative than the bootstrap-percentile criterion: at n = 5 the exact sign-flip test rejects only when all five deltas are positive, which happens about half the time.

type_I_error.method: the observed DEV deltas are sign-randomised so that the cohort-level gradient is zero, then n deltas are drawn; this is the null the v1.6 criterion was never checked against on a properly calibrated scale
type_I_error.reading: the bootstrap-percentile criterion used by v1.6 has a false-positive rate several times the nominal alpha, which is why it cannot serve as a confirmatory criterion. The exact tests are calibrated by construction.

credibility_rule.rule: E2 may remain a CONFIRMATORY criterion only if ALL of: (1) the Type I error at the null is controlled at alpha = 0.05 (not approximated); (2) the test is not degenerate at the evaluable n, i.e. the smallest attainable one-sided p is <= alpha; (3) the power against the DEV participant distribution is at least 0.80. Otherwise E2 becomes DESCRIPTIVE.
reasoning: at n = 4 the exact test is degenerate: its smallest attainable one-sided p is 0.0625 > 0.05, so it can never reject, whatever the data show.

at n = 5 the exact test is valid but weak: rejection requires all five participant deltas to be positive, giving a power of about 0.52 against the DEV participant distribution, far below the 0.80 the rule demands.

the only criterion that would be strong enough is the bootstrap-percentile interval, and that criterion's Type I error is several times the nominal alpha, so it cannot be used for a confirmation claim.

therefore no admissible one-sided test at n <= 5 can carry the activity component as a confirmatory criterion. E2 is reported as a DESCRIPTIVE quantity: point estimate, interval, per-participant deltas, and the exact p-value, with the explicit statement that a null result is UNTESTED rather than refuted.
the rule was fixed before any SEALED value was read and is not revisited after seeing the confirmation result.

C6_cross_project_contact_carried_forward.status: UNCHANGED from v1.6 -- the history is registered, not re-litigated, and the disclosure text is bound into the manuscript
C6_cross_project_contact_carried_forward.required_disclosure_text: Before this study, the raw recordings of four of the six held-out participants (P17, P19, P20, P23) had been processed by an unrelated research project that used the same public GalaxyPPG release for a different purpose and a different participant split. That project derived participant-level sensor statistics (including a coarse whole-session count of the device's HR status codes) and a window-level cache of PPG, E4 and accelerometer features. No paired device-versus-reference heart-rate comparison on this study's window grid was ever formed for these participants, and no activity label was attached to any cached window, so none of the quantities reported here was available from that work. The protocol, the inclusion rules and the analysis plan of this study were fixed before the held-out data were opened, and the confirmation run was executed once, in a single direction, with no re-analysis after the results were seen. We therefore do not describe the held-out cohort as never having been processed, and we do not describe this study as a fully independent replication; it is a single-device, single-protocol measurement study whose confirmation was pre-registered and executed once.
